answer: An e-passport chip makes each extra identity pay $165 for a first-time adult book; a farm running N fakes pays N×$165 and cannot share it because the chip signs each challenge with a key no other book holds. The registry runs a falcon check on the chip, matching its number against an ocean of issued books and confirming the signature. A farm reusing one passport dies by chip-signature dedup at 2: the second use flags both identities and voids both seats, while the reef of verified books keeps one seat per document. One book, one seat.
